category_title: Aboriginal adolescents in alternative education who resist traditional pedagogy but engage with digital multiliteracies
scenario_title: Analyzing author's language and tone in a newspaper article
minimal_context: The student is reading a newspaper article about Aboriginal gangs in an alternative education classroom to analyze the author's tone and language.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's look at the newspaper article about Aboriginal gangs again so we can finish talking about the author's tone and the language they used.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Fair? How can it be fair? They watch us like hawks, like criminals, and not the other kids at break. How come white guys are allowed to walk inside the shop? They can do anything. Nobody is following, and we have the stupid man near us all the time.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's try to focus on the text. Please read the next section on your own so we can look at the audience.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Boring...boring...boring. It’s all stupid. I didn’t come to school to learn this.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: We just need to finish what we started yesterday with the article.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Pushes the newspaper article away) I'm not reading it again. You want to know about gangs? Let's talk about gang clothing, weapons, and initiation rites. That's how gang protection and hierarchies actually work.
